transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-07
Time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Claire Mendoza (Redwood AE); Jordan Patel (Redwood SE); Samir Rao (Redwood CSM); Maya Chen (BlueLeaf Eng Lead); Rajiv Singh (BlueLeaf CTO); Laura Gomez (BlueLeaf Product); Ian Park (BlueLeaf Infra)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC check-in focused on staging provisioning status, access handoff, and initial latency/throughput bench plans. Discussed KMS needs, SOC 2 artifacts, and next steps for a focused benchmark. Some mis-heard terms in transcript; technical details confirmed by SE action item.

Topics:
- Staging access and IAM/service account provisioning
- KMS/HSM and data at rest policies
- Latency & throughput bench plan (1k token, 100 qps profile)
- Fallback plan (hosted vs dedicated) and cost sensitivity
- Next steps and scheduling deep-dive

Action items (short):
- Redwood to share KMS guide + SOC2 link
- SE to run bench with BlueLeaf prompts
- BlueLeaf to provision service account and send prompts

Transcript body:
[00:00] Claire (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we are at 14:00 here. quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya (BlueLeaf): Hey, Maya here.
[00:10] Rajiv (BlueLeaf): Rajiv on the call.
[00:12] Ian (BlueLeaf): Ian, infra.
[00:15] Jordan (Redwood SE): Jordan from Redwood, hi all.
[00:18] Claire: Samir is on too but he might drop for another call. today's agenda: staging provisioning status, KMS discussion, and runplan for the latency bench. anything else to add?
[00:28] Laura (BlueLeaf): maybe quick notes on residency and SSO flow we discussed last week.
[00:31] Claire: yes good call we'll cover SSO at the end.
[00:35] Rajiv: we're mostly blocked on the service account and IP allowlist for the staging cluster, Ian will speak to status.
[00:40] Ian: yeah we spun up the staging VPC but haven't created the service account for Redwood yet — we were waiting for the exact permission set. can you confirm minimal perms?
[00:48] Jordan: minimal perms are basically call-out to the inference endpoint, read-only to certain artifact buckets if you want model assets uploaded, and ability to write logs to the customer audit log endpoint. we will share an IAM policy snippet.
[00:58] Maya: what about key management, our security team insists on using our KMS. can Redwood integrate with external KMS or do we have to hand keys over?
[01:06] Claire: good question — we support customer-managed keys. Jordan, can you cover the KMS flow?
[01:10] Jordan: yeah so Redwood supports both: either you bring a KMS/HSM through our private deployment funnel or we integrate with your cloud KMS via our KMS connector. in the hosted pilot mode we can do envelope encryption where only the customer KMS holds the master key. slight caveat: in some older runtimes we had to do a small shim for key wrapping — but modern stacks are fine.
[01:28] Rajiv: when you say "private deployment funnel" is that the VPC private control plane or full on-prem?
[01:33] Jordan: both. private control plane in a VPC or a fully on-prem package. depends on compliance. for the pilot we can do VPC peering or a transit gateway, whatever you prefer.
[01:41] Ian: transit gateway is preferred. also we need the exact egress IPs to open in our firewall.
[01:46] Claire: we'll provide the IP ranges. action item: Claire to share the IP allowlist and KMS guide.
[01:52] Laura: about logs — does Redwood push audit logs into our log aggregation or do we pull?
[01:57] Samir (Redwood CSM): Samir here — we can push to your syslog/S3 endpoint, or we provide a log export. most customers opt to pull from our audit API, but push is supported.
[02:07] Maya: ok thanks. next, bench plan — Jordan, can you outline the latency/throughput test you suggested?
[02:12] Jordan: sure. plan is a baseline 1k-token prompt, 100 concurrent qps bursts (simulated), measure p50/p95/p99 latency, and tokens/sec throughput. we also want to test cold-cache vs warmed KV cache because BlueLeaf said you will have prefix prompts.
[02:28] Rajiv: we do have a long system prompt — about 300 tokens — and typical user messages ~200 tokens, so the 1k token overall is realistic.
[02:36] Jordan: perfect. also we'll include a run with quantized model variant to compare cost-latency tradeoff.
[02:43] Maya: can Redwood run with our prompt set or do we need to share a sanitized set?
[02:47] Jordan: please share a representative prompt set; sanitized is fine. we'll run the bench in the staging environment you provide, with your data residency controls.
[02:56] Ian: side question: how are KV caches handled in the staging run? do we prewarm?
[03:01] Jordan: we can prewarm KV cache by seeding with representative requests. also we'll run both prewarmed and cold runs. prewarming helps for latency-sensitive paths, but warm cache has different cost profile.
[03:10] Laura: cost profile — can you give us a rough delta between hosted and dedicated for these runs?
[03:15] Claire: high level: dedicated (reserved) gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale; hosted is faster to start but has slightly higher per-token cost. we can share a tailored estimate once Jordan runs the bench and we have your qps profile.
[03:27] Rajiv: our main constraint is latency p95 < 600ms for the 1k token path — is that realistic?
[03:33] Jordan: 600ms p95 for 1k tokens is ambitious but not impossible depending on model size and quantization. for a smaller / quantized model we can approach that; larger dense models will be higher. we'll test variants.
[03:44] Maya: what model family do you recommend for our workload? we prioritize factuality and code-like outputs.
[03:50] Jordan: recommend a mid-sized open model we verified for RL-like code outputs; we'll try both cost-optimized quantized variant and a higher-accuracy float variant. the SE notes in the bench will call out differences.
[03:59] Ian: can we run a throughput run too — e.g., sustained 50 qps for 30 minutes — to check token burn and evictions?
[04:06] Jordan: yes we can. sustained runs are part of the plan. we'll also look at cache eviction and memory pressure in the runtime.
[04:13] Claire: quick check — any blockers for the service account?
[04:17] Ian: just the permission snippet we asked for and I'll provision today.
[04:21] Claire: great. can you confirm a date to provision?
[04:24] Ian: I'll have it by tomorrow EOD, 2026-07-08.
[04:28] Maya: we'll also need the SOC 2 artifacts to feed our compliance flow.
[04:32] Claire: we'll share a SOC 2 summary and our pen test report; Samir will attach the artifact links.
[04:37] Samir: i'll paste the links after the call.
[04:40] Rajiv: curious — did other vendors surface any major differences around KMS? we looked at Anthropic who required additional plumbing last cycle.
[04:47] Claire: some vendors force you to use their key management or require thicker on-prem. Redwood supports cloud KMS integrations which is smoother for most cloud-first customers.
[04:56] Laura: question on SSO — we want SAML and SCIM to provision users. timeline?
[05:01] Claire: SAML + SCIM is part of our enterprise pack; for pilot we can do a manual mapping and later swap to SAML provisioning.
[05:08] Rajiv: fine. one last compliance question: do you support customer-managed logs retention policy? we need 7 years for some records.
[05:16] Jordan: we can configure retention and export to your archive. 7 years is long but export to your archival bucket is the recommended flow.
[05:23] Maya: cool. back to bench specifics: Jordan, will you include per-token cost estimates for each config?
[05:28] Jordan: yes we'll include per-token and per-call economics for quantized vs float models and for caching benefits.
[05:34] Claire: ok let's capture immediate next steps: Claire to share KMS guide and IP allowlist; Jordan to run the bench once staging is provisioned; Ian to provision service account and open firewall; Maya to send prompt set. anything missing?
[05:47] Rajiv: can we get the bench results before next Tues?
[05:50] Jordan: we should be able to run and upload preliminary results by 2026-07-10 if staging is ready by 2026-07-09.
[05:56] Laura: we'll aim to have staging ready on the 9th.
[05:59] Claire: perfect. scheduling: propose a deeper perf deep-dive 2026-07-14 at 10am PT.
[06:06] Maya: works for me.
[06:08] Rajiv: works.
[06:10] Ian: ok.
[06:12] Samir: i'll send calendar invites and the artifact links.
[06:15] Speaker 1: (mumble) — small note, during the bench please ensure you tag runs with the exact model hash; saves us time.
[06:22] Jordan: absolutely, we'll include model hashes and runtime configs.
[06:26] Maya: anything else on the deployment side?
[06:29] Ian: one more item — network egress costs, just want visibility on token outbound.
[06:33] Claire: we'll include estimated egress in the cost table.
[06:36] Laura: thanks.
[06:39] Claire: cool that wraps the main items. recap and we'll follow up: share docs, provision staging, run bench, then deep-dive.
[06:49] Jordan: quick technical clarification after call: we might need to enable an experimental kernel for low-latency inference; it's stable but flagged "opt-in" — we'll note in the bench notes.
[06:58] Maya: fine, just flag it.
[07:01] Rajiv: thanks everyone.
[07:03] Claire: thanks all. ending now.

(End of recording)
